# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

This is a mild reminder, never a gate: in an unattended session, or when it would derail the work at hand, ignore it entirely and leave it for a later interactive session.
- claude-code-web-users-support / store: Where do this project's people keep their personal interaction preferences — the repository holding one `<email>.md` per person? Give an `owner/name` (a fleet usually has one repo for this), or say "n/a — none" if this project has no such store. [distill: the answer's `owner/name` becomes this entry's `config.repo` (add `config.path` only when the files do not sit in `preferences/`); "n/a" leaves the entry without a config and the preferences feature inert]
- executable-requirements / ui_testing: How are the executable UI requirements exercised — what is the UI-testing mechanism (browser/E2E such as Playwright, DOM-level golden rendering, a headless harness), or is there none yet? Most requirements should be verifiable by a short test that drives to a state and makes a VISUAL assertion (a committed golden the owner checks by sight), so this fixes how a requirement becomes that assertion. [distill: recorded as intent; it fixes the harness the requirements.md drives its UI gates through, and the visual-golden path most leaves take for simplest owner verification]
- executable-requirements / requirements_source: Where do the requirements come from — an existing requirements/spec document, the issue tracker, or authored fresh? Name the path or source so the spec is seeded from it rather than reinvented. [distill: record the source; set config.spec to the executable spec's home (default dev/requirements/requirements.md) and extract the initial requirements from the named source]
- product-wiki / product: What is the product — what does it do, and what is the core value it delivers? If the repo already carries a product brief or spec, read it and confirm rather than asking cold. [distill: recorded as intent on this entry (the pack takes no config); it names what the research is about and frames every seeded wiki]
- product-wiki / users: Who are the users or customers — the segments whose needs the research must track? [distill: recorded as intent; scopes the user-research wiki and whose problems the findings answer to]
- product-wiki / market: What market or category is this in, and who are the main competitors or alternatives? This is what the competitor research is scoped against. [distill: recorded as intent; names the competitor set the initial competitor-landscape wiki is seeded from]

100	   node <here>/converge-item.mjs --issue <n> \

113	   suggested: each label set already carries every label the issue should still

124

126	   |---|---|

128	   | `task:status:needs-human-action` | something outside the code must change before this can run: a secret, a scope, a routine's wiring, an input this item never carried |
129	   | `task:status:needs-human-decision` | you stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice — you ran out of time, or you exceeded the declared ceiling and someone must say whether that stands |

   - **Delivered by code-work** names artifacts this run already created — a branch,
     a PR, an issue. Work on those; never make your own duplicates of them.
   - **An input the task file calls required and the issue does not carry stops the
     run.** Say which one was missing and park this item
     (`task:status:needs-human-action` — the item has to be re-created carrying it). Never
     reconstruct it — searching for the issue by title, taking the newest branch, or
     inferring the scope substitutes another run's inputs for this one's, and the run
     then reports success on work nobody asked for.
   - If the work turns out empty, that is a legitimate result. "The work ran and
     produced nothing" is an outcome; deciding not to run is not yours to make.

5. **Verify your outcome in code** against the task's declared ceiling before you
   finish. A `none` task may not open a PR; a task whose `automerge` authorizes
   nothing may not merge one, and a granular policy merges only on the policy
   engine's own `AUTOMERGE: yes` (deliver-pr.md).
   Exceeding the ceiling is a failure, not a success with a surprise.

6. **Converge the issue exactly once — in code, not by hand.** `<here>` in the
   commands below is **the directory this file sits in** —
   `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` in the canon, the same path under
   `.claudinite/shared/` in a member's mount — and `<engine>` is
   `<here>/../../../engine`. Derive both from where you found this file rather
   than from any root you were told.

   **The command decides the transition; you perform it.** It does not touch
   GitHub, and it is not trying to: your GitHub access is yours, and a subprocess
   you spawn cannot reach it. So it plans every side effect the transition needs
   — the comment, the label swap, the outcome label, the `claudinite-task-exec`
   record, the close with the right state reason, the request write-back — and
   prints them as the exact calls to make. That printout **is** the successful
   run.

   Two calls, in this order. First read the item with your own GitHub tools and
   save it as JSON — `issue_read`, method `get` — then:

   ```bash
   node <here>/converge-item.mjs --issue <n> \
     --outcome done|approval|action|decision|failure \
     --summary '<what happened>' [--pr <n>] \
     --repo <owner/name> --item-file <path to that JSON>
   ```

   **You supply the judgment — which outcome, and the prose.** Everything below
   is how to choose; nothing below is yours to perform. If the command refuses,
   read what it says: it means this item is not yours to converge, and doing it
   by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing a live status.

   Then **make the calls it printed, in the order given, changing nothing** — the
   bodies verbatim, the label sets exactly as written. They are computed, not
   suggested: each label set already carries every label the issue should still
   have, so writing your own is how one gets dropped. One step asks you to output
   a line in your reply; do that too, it is the run's only census record.

   | label | when |
   |---|---|
   | `task:status:done` | succeeded, nothing pending — close the issue |
   | a park | anything else — leave the issue open, wearing exactly one of the four below |

   A park is ONE label, and its kind says what you are asking
   a person for. Pick by the REMEDY, not by how the run felt:

   | sub-label | when |
   |---|---|
   | `task:status:needs-human-approval` | you succeeded and deliberately left an unmerged PR. Name it; the human merges or closes it |
   | `task:status:needs-human-action` | something outside the code must change before this can run: a secret, a scope, a routine's wiring, an input this item never carried |
   | `task:status:needs-human-decision` | you stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice — you ran out of time, or you exceeded the declared ceiling and someone must say whether that stands |
   | `task:status:needs-human-failure` | the run broke: a bug, a contract-forbidden shape, a malformed or forged item. Use this when you are unsure |

   **A convergence you could not perform at all is the failure park, and never
   anything else.** Not `decision` (that is for a choice you stopped in front
   of), not `action` (that is for something outside the code that must change
   first). This is not a judgment call: the failure park is the only one that
   HOLDS THE TASK'S LANE, and a run that could not converge must stop its task
   recurring until a person has looked. Choosing a lane-releasing park here is
   how one broken convergence became fourteen stranded items in a member repo,
   one a night, each looking like a fresh incident.

   **Pass `--pr` on any park a pull request or an issue would end**, not only on an
   approval, where it is required. It stamps `Ends-when: #<n> closed` on the item, and
   that is what makes the park end by itself: the janitor closes the item `done` when
   the target merges and `rejected` when it is closed unmerged. Without it the park
   stands until a person happens to read it.

   **A marked issue needs no write-back at all**: it is the item, so the approval
   park it wears *is* the in-review state and the failure park *is* the report (which
   is why `--pr` is still required on an approval — a park nobody can act on is not
   a park). The standing status is also what stops the next scheduler run adopting
   the same issue again; clearing it is a person's decision, made after reading what
   the run said. Only an item filed under the older shadow model writes back to a
   different issue, and the command does that too.

   Only `task:status:needs-human-failure` (and a park whose kind cannot be decoded) holds the
   task's lane — while one is open the generator files no further occurrence of
   this task. The other three wait for their human while the schedule carries on,
   so leaving one open costs nobody but the person it names.

   The `claudinite-task-exec` record goes onto the item, in the same comment, and
   the command writes it — Actions logs expire and the item does not, so the item
   is where a record has to live. Nothing here is yours to print by hand.

7. **Capture this session before you end it.** Last step, after the item is
   converged, and run it whichever way step 6 went:

   ```bash
   CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE=<n> node <engine>/hooks/session-end-command.mjs
   ```

   That runner invokes whatever session-end steps this repo's declared packs
   contribute; it knows nothing about what any of them do, and a repo that
   contributes none does nothing. Nobody is sitting in front of this session, so it
   ends by having its container reclaimed — precisely the ending that fires no
   `SessionEnd` hook. Left to the hook, every unattended run would leave no record
   of itself anywhere: not of the skills it loaded, not of the checks that caught
   something, not of how the work actually went, and not of the record you just
   printed. `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE` is what files those logs under the item that
   ran, rather than under nothing.

   It cannot fail your run — the item is already converged and this changes nothing
   on GitHub. If it reports an error, **say so plainly in your final message** and
   end anyway.

## The one standing bound

You execute **this one item and nothing else**. Never list other work items,
never sweep the queue, never act on a second issue in this session — however
obviously stuck another one looks. Recovery is code that runs elsewhere, and a
session that helps out is how one item becomes three duplicate PRs.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# tidy-issues worker

The **acting** half of the repo tidy-up: triage the issues in scope, then record what you did. The run's
**Context section is binding scope** — it lists the issues to triage. Work only those; don't enumerate the
repo yourself. GitHub access is **MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`).

This task writes **issues only** (its triage actions and its own tracker). It never opens, closes, merges,
or comments on a PR — that dimension belongs to `tidy-prs`, which is assess-only.

## 1. Triage each issue

For each issue in the Context list, run the [single-issue-triage](../../skills/single-issue-triage/SKILL.md)
skill. The skill owns the action ladder and the safeguards: "implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual
ask is true of `main`'s content **now** — verified there and cited, never inferred — and when the check is
inconclusive it **comments, doesn't close** — and an issue whose verdict is the one the skill
already posted there returns `unchanged`, written to nowhere. Collect what each triage did.

## 2. Reconcile this task's tracker

**Only a run that changed something reaches the tracker.** What counts is a triage action actually taken —
an issue closed, a comment posted — or something this run leaves for a human. `left` and
`unchanged` are not actions. A run that worked its whole Context list and took no action has
**nothing to record**: leave the tracker exactly as found, no body rewrite and no comment, and
create none if it doesn't exist. The scan itself is not news.

One standing tracker issue per repo, titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues` — found by that
**exact title, never a fuzzy match**; create it **already closed** when there is something to record and it
is absent — creation always lands an issue open and ignores a `state: closed` argument, so create it and
close it in a second call (never a fresh issue per run, never a bare number that can dangle). Each dimension
keeps its **own** tracker, so the two tasks never race to rewrite one body.

Touch it two ways on a run that has something to record:

- **Rewrite the issue body** to today's **dated** snapshot: the actions taken this run and anything left
  for a human. The body is the live picture — it replaces yesterday's, it doesn't accumulate.
- **Add a dated comment** with today's status, so the body's snapshots leave a per-run trail.

Keep both short. **Never open, close, or reopen the tracker** — its state carries no meaning (the body is
the live picture; the state is just however it was created).

## 3. Retire the legacy tracker (transitional, one line of work)

Repos tidied before the split carry a single combined tracker titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Repo
Tidy`. If it exists and its body doesn't already say so, rewrite the body to one line pointing at the
per-dimension trackers (`Tidy Issues`, `Tidy PRs`) and stop there — nothing else to do on it, and never
open, close, or reopen it. Already pointing at them ⇒ skip. Absent ⇒ skip; never create it.

`model: sonnet` — the implemented-in-`main` call is judgment; the reconcile is mechanical aggregation.


Base directory for this skill: /home/user/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/.claude/skills/single-issue-triage

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

{"number":1103,"title":"Chrome Web Store release pipeline is a generation behind the chrome-extension pack","body":"`cer/release-workflows` reports two blocking findings against `main`, and reading the drift out in full shows the repo is running the pre-`bump` generation of the pack's release standard rather than being two files short of the current one.

They only surface at the Stop hook: this repo's CI runs `test`, not `check_the_world`, which is why `main` has been sitting red on them (#648 is the open issue for adding that job).

## What the checks say

```
[BLOCKING] cer/release-workflows  .github/workflows/chrome-extension-release.yml
  does not call the local reusable workflow ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-bump-version.yml

[BLOCKING] cer/release-workflows  .github/workflows/chrome-extension-bump-version.yml
  vendored reusable workflow chrome-extension-bump-version.yml is missing
```

## What is actually different

Comparing each `.github/workflows/` file against `.claudinite/shared/packs/chrome-extension/stubs/workflows/`:

| file | state |
|---|---|
| `chrome-extension-bump-version.yml` | **absent** — `mode: bump` (the deliberate minor/major raise) does not exist in this repo |
| `chrome-extension-release.yml` | pre-`bump` orchestrator: no `bump` job, no `ref` passthrough into create-package, `mode` choices are `publish/package/daily` only |
| `chrome-extension-daily-release.yml` | ~157 changed lines — the release trigger moved from *"did a shipped file change since the last release"* to *"has the version on `main` been released yet"* |
| `chrome-extension-create-package.yml` | 4 changed lines |
| `chrome-extension-publish-store.yml` | 6 changed lines |
| `.github/release.config` | header says "all six keys" and lists five; the current standard declares five |

The daily-release change is the substantive one. The pack's standard is now *the version comes from the change*: a PR touching a shipped file raises the patch in the same PR (`cer/version-bumped`), so merging it is what cuts the release, and create-package no-ops unless the version on `main` has no release yet. This repo still diffs shipped paths against the latest release tag instead.

## Not a finding

The orchestrator carrying **no** `schedule:` trigger is correct and should stay that way. The pack stub ships `cron: "30 0 * * *"` for extension repos with no Claudinite scheduler; a scheduler-running repo like this one is required to drop it, because the canon `chrome-extension/store-release` task fires the daily leg and the scheduler stays the repo's only cron. `store-release` itself is current — `expected_outcome: 'none'`, byte-identical to canon HEAD.

## What closing this takes

Re-vendor the workflow set from `stubs/workflows/` (de-cronned), add the missing `chrome-extension-bump-version.yml`, reconcile `.github/release.config` against the five-key standard, and confirm `cer/release-workflows` goes silent. It changes what ships and when — the new `bump` mode writes a version and pushes it — so it wants its own reviewed PR and a deliberate look at the first release cut under the new semantics, rather than riding along with unrelated work.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/1103","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-30T21:18:11Z","updated_at":"2026-08-30T21:18:11Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":648,"title":"Add a Claudinite conformance-checks job to CI (backstop for the Stop hook)","body":"## Problem

This repo runs the Claudinite conformance checks only via the **Stop hook** (Claude Code sessions). CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) does **not** run `node .claudinite/checks/run.mjs`, so a violation introduced outside a session — a human edit on GitHub web, or any non-session change — isn't caught by CI.

This surfaced during #646: the bespoke `shared-constants` uber test used to run inside `npm test` (so GCEC CI guarded those 8 constants on every PR). Retiring it in favor of Claudinite's canonical `shared-constants` check moved that enforcement to the Stop hook only. The canonical check is strictly better, but without a CI job it isn't a CI-level gate anymore.

## Fix

Add a CI job that runs the Claudinite check sweep (`node .claudinite/checks/run.mjs`) on PRs/pushes — the "CI is the backstop" job from Claudinite's design that this repo never picked up. It restores CI coverage for the migrated constants **and** adds it for every other Claudinite universal/tech-pack check (reference integrity, workflow lints, squash-merge history, etc.) — a net gain over the pre-#646 state.

Note the sequencing detail the check runner already documents: CI must ensure `.claudinite/` is populated (Method B tarball sync or submodule) before running the sweep.

Refs #646.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/648","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":17,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-07T12:12:24Z","updated_at":"2026-08-17T05:57:36Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":679,"title":"Proof of concept: move local capture into Claudinite local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/)","body":"Claudinite is gaining first-class **per-project packs**: a tracked `.claudinite/local_packs//` root inside each consumer, carrying the full pack surface — prose rules (`RULES.md`), checks, `run_daily` tasks, and skills — discovered and run by the same engine as canon packs (prose injection at SessionStart, checks at Stop/CI, skill mounting, the fleet daily planner).

This repo is the proof of concept: restructure the existing local capture surface (`dev/procedures/*.md` working docs, `dev/routines/*`) into two local packs so the owner can review the target shape as a folder structure instead of a design doc:

- `.claudinite/local_packs/gcec/` — the project's general working pack (rules prose, a first real conformance check, snapshot-approval / merge-and-ci / testing-guide skills)
- `.claudinite/local_packs/extractor-pipeline/` — the extractor domain pack (the create-extractor and auto-fallback-coverage routines as `run_daily` tasks, the add-live-case skill, pipeline rules)

The PoC branch intentionally lands **before** the Claudinite engine support (pack discovery second scan root, sync-hook preserve, planner integration, migration); it must not merge until that support ships upstream.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/679","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"assignees":[],"comments":17,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-15T08:38:01Z","updated_at":"2026-08-16T13:51:52Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":749,"title":"product-requirements/README.md cites dev/procedures/technicalGotchas.md, which no longer exists","body":"Found during the 2026-07-26 product-wiki growth pass (#739, PR #745) while spot-checking citations the recent `dev/procedures/` → gcec-local-pack move may have superseded.

**The dead reference**

`product-wiki/product-requirements/README.md` line 60 cites `dev/procedures/technicalGotchas.md`'s `ctz`-derivation rule. That file no longer exists — per `.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/README.md`, the pack "replaced the always-`@`-imported `dev/procedures/{workflow,github,testing,technicalGotchas}.md` docs". `dev/procedures/` now contains only `fileDescriptions.md` and `highLevelDesign.md`.

{"number":430,"title":"Add a daily automated UI-test improvement routine (with its own doc + tracking issue)","body":"## Goal

Add a daily unattended Claude **Opus** routine that tries to improve the **UI snapshot tests** — the counterpart of the existing daily routines (lessons `#365`, fallback-coverage `#366`, branch-report `#399`), each of which keeps its instructions in a repo doc and logs runs to its own standing tracking issue.

This routine runs **fully offline** on a fresh clone (the sandbox can't fetch live pages or run Chrome) and, like the others, **most days correctly changes nothing**.

## What it looks for

A genuinely useful, *true* improvement to the UI test suite, e.g.:

- **Claim accuracy** — a case that claims a requirement its snapshot can't actually verify (behavioral/unreachable leaves, the class found in the audit issue this references). Surface or re-home it.
- **Coverage honesty** — a leaf parked on a snapshot that should instead be a unit test on the view logic.
- **Missing rendering cases** — a leaf requirement whose visible rendering isn't actually pinned by any PNG, or a real rendering variation no case exercises.
- **Case simplification** — an over-complex case that could be split/trimmed per `docs/claude/testing.md` ("keep integration/UI cases as simple as possible").

## Scope / guardrails

- **Offline only**; deterministic. Touches `test/ui/**`, `ui/views/**` tests, and `docs/uiRequirements.md` claims — never ships popup behavior changes.
- An intentional pixel change must follow the **expected-vs-actual approval gate** (`docs/claude/workflow.md`) — never auto-accept a moved snapshot.
- Red-before-green; full suite green; regenerate `test/ui/README.md` via `npm run refresh:ui`.
- **PR for review, never a merge.** No real improvement → no branch, no PR.

## Plumbing (match the existing routines)

- New spec doc `docs/claude/auto-ui-tests.md`, imported from `CLAUDE.md`, written as the routine's source of truth; the launcher is a thin pointer to it (`docs/agenticBestPractices.md`).
- Its own standing tracking issue (find **by title**, reopen if closed), logging each PR-producing run as a **dated comment** — one issue per routine, per `docs/claude/auto-lessons.md` / `docs/agenticBestPractices.md`.
- Reference the audit issue (the companion to this one) as the seed backlog of known UI-test gaps.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/430","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"assignees":[],"comments":14,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-06-19T21:48:59Z","updated_at":"2026-08-16T13:50:58Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":438,"title":"Add a periodic "edge-case review" routine for the UI requirements","body":"A recurring (daily, Opus, Claude Code) routine that periodically re-reads `docs/uiRequirements.md` and the popup rendering code and **hunts for edge cases the requirements don't yet pin** — then either generates a `_(TBD)_` placeholder requirement (with a provisional snapshot of current behavior) for review, or, where the behavior is settled, generates the missing test. This is a thinking pass that should run regularly so gaps surface instead of accumulating silently.

### Why
This came out of a manual review pass that immediately turned up several uncovered/under-specified edge cases:
- **4.2.3** — cross-month grouping: one event with a Jun 15 instance, a Jun 28→Jul 3 *spanning* instance, and a Jul 10 instance. Today the span groups by its start (June only); should it also surface under July? (now a `_(TBD)_`).
- **4.10** — a single instance spanning multiple months: chip shows the start day only; should a long span show a date range on the calendar chip? (now a `_(TBD)_`).
- **5.7.3** — a grouped all-day card's header renders location-only; should it read "All day · location"? (now a `_(TBD)_`).
- **4.9** — the snapshot only checked card ordering, not within-card showing ordering (the second half of the requirement). Fixed this pass.
- **4.4** — "clickable" can't be shown by a cursor in the static renderer; a DOM assertion (the element is a `` whose computed `cursor` is `pointer`) belongs in a unit test. Candidate work item for this routine.

### Mechanics to mirror
Follow the existing daily-routine pattern (thin launcher pointing at an in-repo doc; its own standing tracking issue logging each run as dated comments; opens a PR, never merges) — see `docs/claude/auto-lessons.md`, `docs/claude/auto-fallback-coverage.md`, `docs/claude/auto-branch-report.md`. Add a `docs/claude/auto-edge-cases.md` spec and a standing tracking issue when it's built.

The `_(TBD)_` requirement kind (placeholder, exempt from the snapshot bijection, rendered with a "TO BE DECIDED" banner + optional provisional snapshot) already exists as of #436, so this routine has a place to put its findings.

{"number":748,"title":"Scheduler appears to be firing multiple concurrent executor sessions against the same dispatch issues","body":"While running today's executor pass (2026-07-26), the `repo-tidy` subagent dispatched for issue #740 discovered its own work had already been done — twice — by other session(s) earlier in the same short window, before it ever started:

- The `Claudinite tracker: Repo Tidy` issue (#695) had already been rewritten twice (comments at 04:10:52 and 04:13:21 UTC) with a snapshot matching what this run independently arrived at.
- Direct triage comments already existed on #727, #724, #616, #617 (posted ~04:10–04:11 UTC) from whatever ran before it.

My own executor session labeled #740 `agent-running` and dispatched its repo-tidy subagent shortly after 04:07 UTC — so at least one other actor reached the same issue and did the same read-only assessment + issue re-confirmation independently, in parallel, within minutes. The duplicate work itself was harmless here (read-only re-confirmations, no new closes, no PR actions), but it's wasted subagent time and a real race: if a future task's work were less idempotent (e.g. one that *does* act on a PR), concurrent dispatches against the same issue could conflict or double-act.

Worth checking:
- Whether the `issues.labeled` webhook is spawning a separate executor session per label event *in addition to* the scheduled/cron-triggered executor session — each independently sweeping the full `ready-for-agent` backlog (executor.md step 1's "collect the work list, process every other open ready-for-agent issue" self-healing sweep), so a single scheduler run that files N dispatch issues could trigger up to N+1 concurrent executor sessions all racing to claim the same N issues.
- Whether the claim step (`ready-for-agent` → `agent-running` label swap) has a race window that lets two sessions both see `ready-for-agent` before either's swap lands.

Separately, unrelated but noted again in the same tracker snapshot: issue #615 still duplicates #695's exact tracker title (from 2026-07-20) and wants consolidating — flagged before, still open.

The routine tries to make the **generic** fallback extractor recover more of what the dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the fallback-coverage gate, and opens a **PR for review** only on a clean, generic, test-covered win (most runs correctly change nothing).

Each run that produces a PR logs it here as a new **dated comment** — not a sub-issue — and references this issue (`Refs #366`), so the routine's output accumulates in one scrollable feed for reviewing it and spotting when the routine itself needs tuning.

**Long-lived**, found **by title**: if it's ever **closed**, the routine **reopens it** when a run next needs logging.

Full spec: [`docs/claude/auto-fallback-coverage.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/blob/main/docs/claude/auto-fallback-coverage.md). Replaces the single umbrella idea in #360 (closed): each daily routine gets its own log. [{"id":5082021796,"body":"Stronger evidence, from converging the other three dispatches (#738, #739, #741) after this issue was filed — every single one of them independently hit the same symptom, and it's worse than "wasted read-only re-confirmation":

- **#741 (fallback-extractor-improvements) produced three separate PRs** — #750, #751, #752 — all `Refs #741`, all based off the same `main` commit, each a *different* independent generic win in the same file family (`derive-timezone.js` / `embedded-events.js` / the GENERATED coverage artifacts). Deliberate departures: `extension-test/integration/` for whole-extension/interaction tests; no mirror for `custom/*` sources or data/markup files (covered by live cases / snapshots / drift guards); `extension-test/harness.js` is shared infra (not a test) and stays at the root."

Checked the rule against the real tree (`git ls-files`) before writing anything, per the check-the-world discipline. A literal 1:1 mirror check would red today's correct `main`:

- `extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js`, `assemble-events.js`, `registry.js`, and most of `helpers/*.js` (`dates.js`, `dom.js`, `embedded-events.js`, `merge.js`, `text.js`, `timezone-names.js`, `timezones.js`) have **no individual test file** — they're covered collectively by `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js` (and `registry.js` additionally by `extension-test/integration/registry-idempotent.test.js`). - `extension/config.js` has no test file at all and isn't a `custom/*` source; whether it counts as the prose's "data/markup" exemption is itself a judgment call (it's a real `.js` module with exported logic, not markup/JSON).

So the prose's exemption list doesn't match how the tree is actually organized — the real invariant is looser than stated (per-area consolidation is allowed for `event-extractors/`, `config.js` is exempt too), and encoding that as a check means guessing at exemptions the prose never names rather than asserting its literal form.
